target_customer: People with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, free to them; revenue is planned from health plans, employers and researchers per the company site.
problem: People with IBD lack a good way to log symptoms, diet and treatment and to see patterns over time to share with clinicians.
business_model: Free consumer app with planned B2B revenue from health plans, employers and researchers; the App Store lists in-app purchases
product_category: Digital health, chronic condition self-management app

founders.name: Max Williamson
founders.background_notes: YC page: AI and global health work at Rockefeller, foreign policy fellow in the US Senate, data director for a Senate campaign, helped launch a COVID testing lab in Delaware; Truman Scholar and Rhodes finalist.

founders.name: Peter Crocker
prior_employers: Several biotech companies as an ML researcher
education: MIT, BA 2020 and MEng 2021 in electrical engineering and computer science

founders.name: Greg Miller
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a former founder, a policy entrepreneur. The launch post also credits the team with past roles at HUD, not attributed per person.

competitors.name: My IBD Care
competitors.what: Symptom tracking, personal health record and self-management courses for Crohn's and colitis, with a clinician portal
competitors.traction_then: Trialled in 2017 with 54 people at King's College Hospital; a 2023 review rated it highest in quality among the apps assessed
competitors.funding_then: Developed by Ampersand Health with Crohn's & Colitis UK under an Innovate UK funded study

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile logging app with clinical severity indices and an LLM layer for pattern finding. Standard consumer app engineering; clinical score calculation adds care but not research risk.

defensibility.rationale: Longitudinal patient logs could become a data asset, but symptom trackers for IBD already existed and the app is free, so the product was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action against the company was found in the sources opened.

market_need_then: The founders say a friend with IBD insisted no decent apps existed. A review cited in search results found most IBD apps lacked clinician input and guideline coverage.

branding.domain_note: Uses aidyhq.com, the name plus a suffix, not the exact .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, patient-friendly; states it is not medical advice.

branding.community_and_virality: Listed on the Crohn's and Colitis Foundation helpful apps page according to one unverified search summary.

brand_strength.rationale: Three names in 2025 and little press on the brand itself; the Aidy name also appeared on the YC page for an earlier grants product. Brand was not yet established.

pivots.from: Federal grant application tool (Aidy Grants, per the YC launch post)
pivots.to: IBD symptom and treatment tracking app
pivots.why: The long description says the team went through a lengthy pivot hell before listening to a friend with IBD; exact dates are not given.

outcome_analysis: The company is active as a two to ten person team. After a long pivot period it settled on an IBD tracking app, launching under three names during 2025 before settling on Aidy in October 2025. No traction figures or verified funding were found, so the story is still early and cannot be classed as success or stall.
notes: Aggregators report a $500K seed in 2024 with Y Combinator and SSBXi; one directory says no Form D appears in EDGAR. Treated as unverified, no round recorded. The competitor entry is dated by a 2023 review, not by a launch article. Cara Care was also found but no dated source near the batch. The Aidy company site confirms the rename dates (Gut Hero July 2025, Aidy October 2025). Completeness pass: Round rests on databases only (CB Insights: $500K convertible note dated 2024-04-04; Seedtable-style listings call it seed, VCBacked pre-seed). No Form D found in EDGAR.
